summary:
This law cancels a rule from the Department of Energy. The Department of Energy is a government agency that deals with energy rules.

The canceled rule was about the Energy Conservation Program for appliance standards. It covered certification, labels, and enforcement for some home products and business equipment. Certification means companies may have to show that a product meets rules. Labels can give information about a product. Enforcement means how the government checks and handles rule-breaking.

Congress used a law called chapter 8 of title 5 of the United States Code to reject the rule. This is a process that lets Congress disapprove certain agency rules.

The rule was published in the Federal Register on October 9, 2024. The Federal Register is where the government posts official rules and notices.

Because this law was approved on May 9, 2025, the Department of Energy rule “shall have no force or effect.” That means the rule is not in effect and cannot be used.
